messages:
maria: quick sync — CI started failing on a few repos when installing deps for the python SDK (poetry -> export -> pip freeze flow). mypy says AsyncClient has no attribute 'stream' (weird typing mismatch)
kevin: can you paste the mypy error and the install steps? sounds like a stubs mismatch or multiple package versions installed at once
maria: here's the minimal error: 
```
error: "RedwoodClient" has no attribute "stream" (reportGeneralTypeIssues)
   --> src/app/clients.py:42
42 |     async for chunk in client.chat.stream(..):
   |                          ^
```
 also reproduction steps: we export requirements.txt from poetry locks and use a constraints.txt from pip-compile, then CI runs `pip install -r requirements.txt --constraint constraints.txt`
sam: common culprits: typing-extensions version, multiple installs of redwood SDK (wheel vs editable), or an older stub file from a transitive dep. did you end up with two different redwood packages in the env?
maria: I inspected pip list in failing CI — shows `redwood-sdk 0.12.3` and `redwood-client-stubs 0.9.0` (??) — stubs came from a third-party package.
jenny: oh that explains it, stubs mismatching runtime API. either remove the stub dependency or align versions. quick fix is to pin or add an explicit `redwood-client-stubs==0.12.3` or just remove the stub package from the constraints file
kevin: another approach: prefer binary wheels so you don't accidentally get an older sdist that has different packaging metadata: `pip install --prefer-binary --constraint constraints.txt -r requirements.txt`
sam: if CI uses manylinux or custom wheel cache — ensure wheel build step isn't producing stale wheels. `pip wheel --no-deps -r requirements.txt -w /tmp/wheels` then install from that wheel dir in CI can make installs deterministic
maria: also saw streaming code causing runtime-only errors when using older asyncio types. example of how we recommend using the client: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def run():
    async with RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) as client:
        async for evt in client.chat.stream(model="gpt-like", messages=msgs):
            print(evt.delta)
```
```
# common mistake: calling the coroutine directly (sync for) -> returns coroutine object, mypy confuses the two
async for evt in client.chat.stream(...):  # correct
for evt in client.chat.stream(...):        # wrong
```
jenny: also check the SDK extras — we ship optional typing extras and an `async` extra that pulls in right runtime. installing `redwood[async]` can ensure the async types are present
kevin: regarding poetry -> pip export: recommend also exporting a constraints file with hashes so pip can't downgrade back to older deps. pip-compile + `--generate-hashes` works for that flow
sam: for local dev + CI parity, enforce `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools` before installing — older pip can prefer sdists and produce surprising installs
maria: thanks — one weirdness I hit: mypy still complained until I pinned `typing-extensions==4.6.3`. no idea why, but changing that fixed the annotation resolution in our job
jenny: typing-extensions is a frequent footgun across py3.8-3.11 mixes. document that in the repo's CONTRIBUTING.md as a recommended constraint
kevin: follow-up: if anyone hits streaming quirks where the generator yields bytes vs dicts, check whether the project installed `redwood-streaming-compat` or a fallback shim. sometimes the fallback exposes a different runtime shape
maria: created a tiny reproducer and opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood/example-repros/issues/78 — includes requirements.txt, constraints.txt, and a minimal mypy config
devex-bot: created issue DEVEX-3421: investigate poetry export -> pip constraints type mismatch (linked to github issue) :robot_face:
sam: action items: 1) pin typing-extensions in our example constraints, 2) add a short note in devex playbook about `pip --prefer-binary` and wheel pinning, 3) add CONTRIBUTING.md blurb about avoiding stray stub packages
jenny: I can send a tiny PR to add the blurb and update the example constraints.json in the templates repo
maria: thanks all. if someone can review the PR quickly would be great — tagging @kevin for review. I'll add the reproducer link to the PR too
kevin: happy to review later today. :thumbsup:
